PULSATING DC - Is a current that varies in amplitude but does not reverse polarity. It is not a steady direct current because its value fluctuates. However, it is not alternating current because the polarity remains the same, either positive or negative.
DEFINITION
The rectifier output is pulsating DC that has a ripple frequency.
The rectifier section of a power supply is where AC is converted to DC power.

Let's begin the lesson on BRIDGE RECTIFIER OPERATION......................
Using the same transformer without the center tap, the output is twice that of a full wave rectifier.
The advantage of a bridge rectifier over a full wave rectifier is that the applied voltage is taken across the full potential of the transformer.
Bridge rectifiers convert AC power into pulsating DC power just like full wave rectifiers.
In this lesson, you will learn about the operation of bridge rectifier circuits.
